locators.excerpt:
An unsplittable b-transshipment is a b-transshipment together with a path
decomposition consisting of source–sink paths only, and with at most one path for each
source–sink pair.
locators.label: Transshipment and unsplittability definitions

locators.excerpt:
We are given an acyclic digraph
D = (V, A) with a set of sources S⁺ and a set of sinks S⁻, together with supplies and
demands specified by a balance function b : V → ℝ and a fractional b-transshipment x.
locators.label: Acyclic digraph context

locators.excerpt:
Whether arc-wise upper and lower bounds can
be achieved simultaneously remains an intriguing open question, even in the special SSUF
case.
locators.label: Open-status paragraph

locators.excerpt:
Conjecture 12. Given a b-transshipment x, one can efficiently compute an unsplittable
b-transshipment y such that

x_a − d_max ≤ y_a ≤ x_a + d_max for all a ∈ A.
locators.label: Conjecture 12

source_documents.title: Unsplittable Transshipments
source_documents.venue: 53rd International Colloquium on Automata, Languages, and Programming (ICALP 2026), LIPIcs 374, Article 74

caveats: Separate one-sided upper and lower bounds are proved; the simultaneous two-sided guarantee is what remains conjectural.
The frozen target preserves the acyclic-network context used by the paper's Modified DGG framework.

The experimental target additionally requires b not to be identically zero, so the source's maximum sink demand is defined, and restricts real-valued data to exact rational inputs. The rational-input target is a strictly narrower computational operationalization, not an equivalent restatement of the full real-domain conjecture.

records.target: For every finite acyclic digraph D=(V,A), nonzero rational balance function b:V->Q with sum_v b(v)=0, and nonnegative rational b-transshipment x satisfying sum_{a out of v} x_a - sum_{a into v} x_a = b(v) for every v, compute in polynomial time a nonnegative b-transshipment y admitting a weighted decomposition into directed source-to-sink paths with at most one positive-weight path for each ordered source-sink pair, such that x_a-d_max <= y_a <= x_a+d_max for every arc a, where sources have b>0, sinks have b<0, and d_max=max_{t:b(t)<0}|b(t)|. This rational-input statement is a bit-model operationalization narrower than the source's literal real-valued domain; prove or rigorously disprove this exact operationalized claim.
records.title: Two-sided arc bounds for unsplittable transshipments
